title.value: Learning Representations for New Sound Classes With Continual Self-Supervised Learning
title.justification: The title is directly mentioned in the beginning of the paper.
title.quote: Learning Representations for New Sound Classes With Continual Self-Supervised Learning arXiv:2205.07390v2 [eess.AS] ^{13} ^{Dec} ^{2022}

extractions.description: This paper focuses on developing a sound recognition system that can continually incorporate new sound classes without relying heavily on labeled data. By adopting self-supervised representation learning, the authors propose a method that is robust to catastrophic forgetting. The approach involves training an encoder using unlabeled data, then finetuning a classifier for specific tasks. The proposed method aims to improve continual learning by making it less prone to forgetting and computationally efficient.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not directly relate to any of the predefined eco-responsible categories. It discusses methodologies for continual learning and sound recognition systems, focusing on algorithmic development rather than environmental impacts or applications.
primary_category.quote: In this paper, we work on a sound recognition system that continually incorporates new sound classes. Our main goal is to develop a framework where the model can be updated without relying on labeled data.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper's focus is on machine learning algorithms rather than environmental or sustainability topics, which is why no secondary category is applicable.
secondary_categories.quote: These continual learning methods are applied in the image domain, however, continual learning has potential applications in speech and audio processing systems as well, including personal voice assistants, and conversational AI agents.

primary_sub_category.justification: The content of the paper does not align with any sub-category focused on environmental or ecological topics. Its primary focus is on advancing machine learning techniques for sound classification.
primary_sub_category.quote: In the space of incorporating representation learning within a continual learning setup, recent works include [35]–[38]. Different from this paper, these works are applied to images and involve explicit ways to combat catastrophic forgetting.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: Similar to the primary sub-category, no secondary eco-responsible sub-categories apply as the paper focuses on machine learning techniques.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: These early works on self-supervised learning focused on images and natural language processing. Only recently has self-supervised learning been extended to audio and speech as well

applications.justification: The application of the methodologies discussed in this paper is primarily for improving sound classification systems, making them more adaptive and efficient by using continual and self-supervised learning techniques.
applications.quote: These continual learning methods are applied in the image domain, however, continual learning has potential applications in speech and audio processing systems as well, including personal voice assistants, and conversational AI agents.

new_primary_category.justification: A new category suggested because the paper focuses on advancing methods in self-supervised learning and continual learning, primarily within the domain of sound classification.
new_primary_category.quote: Adopting representation learning for continual learning of new sound classes enables the study of the practically interesting case where only a small amount of labels is present.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: A new sub-category focused on the development and application of continual learning algorithms, especially in the context of self-supervised learning for sound classification.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: We propose using similarity-based self-supervised algorithms for representation learning in this framework, and we call this approach continual self-supervised representation learning (CSSL).
